raw_tools.name: emulate

latitude.description: Latitude between -90 and 90.

longitude.description: Longitude between -180 and 180.

geolocation.description: Geolocation to emulate. Set to null to clear the geolocation override.

uid.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot

args.description: An optional list of arguments to pass to the function.

raw_tools.name: performance_analyze_insight
raw_tools.description: Provides more detailed information on a specific Performance Insight of an insight set that was highlighted in the results of a trace recording.

insightSetId.description: The id for the specific insight set. Only use the ids given in the "Available insight sets" list.

insightName.description: The name of the Insight you want more information on. For example: "DocumentLatency" or "LCPBreakdown"

raw_tools.name: performance_start_trace
raw_tools.description: Starts a performance trace recording on the selected page. This can be used to look for performance problems and insights to improve the performance of the page. It will also report Core Web Vital (CWV) scores for the page.

reload.description: Determines if, once tracing has started, the page should be automatically reloaded.

autoStop.description: Determines if the trace recording should be automatically stopped.

raw_tools.name: performance_stop_trace
raw_tools.description: Stops the active performance trace recording on the selected page.

raw_tools.name: press_key
raw_tools.description: Press a key or key combination. Use this when other input methods like fill() cannot be used (e.g., keyboard shortcuts, navigation keys, or special key combinations).

key.description: A key or a combination (e.g., "Enter", "Control+A", "Control++", "Control+Shift+R"). Modifiers: Control, Shift, Alt, Meta

raw_tools.name: resize_page
raw_tools.description: Resizes the selected page's window so that the page has specified dimension

width.description: Page width

height.description: Page height

raw_tools.name: select_page
raw_tools.description: Select a page as a context for future tool calls.

pageIdx.description: The index of the page to select. Call list_pages to get available pages.

bringToFront.description: Whether to focus the page and bring it to the top.

raw_tools.name: take_screenshot
raw_tools.description: Take a screenshot of the page or element.

format.description: Type of format to save the screenshot as. Default is "png"

quality.description: Compression quality for JPEG and WebP formats (0-100). Higher values mean better quality but larger file sizes. Ignored for PNG format.

uid.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot. If omitted takes a pages screenshot.

fullPage.description: If set to true takes a screenshot of the full page instead of the currently visible viewport. Incompatible with uid.

filePath.description: The absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory, to save the screenshot to instead of attaching it to the response.

raw_tools.name: take_snapshot
raw_tools.description:
Take a text snapshot of the currently selected page based on the a11y tree. The snapshot lists page elements along with a unique
identifier (uid). Always use the latest snapshot. Prefer taking a snapshot over taking a screenshot. The snapshot indicates the element selected

verbose.description: Whether to include all possible information available in the full a11y tree. Default is false.

filePath.description: The absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory, to save the snapshot to instead of attaching it to the response.

pageId.description: The ID of the page to select. Call list_pages to get available pages.

bringToFront.description: Whether to focus the page and bring it to the top.

raw_tools.name: take_memory_snapshot
raw_tools.description: Capture a memory heapsnapshot of the currently selected page to memory leak debugging

filePath.description: A path to a .heapsnapshot file to save the heapsnapshot to.

raw_tools.name: take_screenshot
raw_tools.description: Take a screenshot of the page or element.

format.description: Type of format to save the screenshot as. Default is "png"

quality.description: Compression quality for JPEG and WebP formats (0-100). Higher values mean better quality but larger file sizes. Ignored for PNG format.

uid.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot. If omitted takes a pages screenshot.

fullPage.description: If set to true takes a screenshot of the full page instead of the currently visible viewport. Incompatible with uid.

filePath.description: The absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory, to save the screenshot to instead of attaching it to the response.

raw_tools.name: take_snapshot
raw_tools.description:
Take a text snapshot of the currently selected page based on the a11y tree. The snapshot lists page elements along with a unique
identifier (uid). Always use the latest snapshot. Prefer taking a snapshot over taking a screenshot. The snapshot indicates the element selected
in the DevTools Elements panel (if any).

verbose.description: Whether to include all possible information available in the full a11y tree. Default is false.

filePath.description: The absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory, to save the snapshot to instead of attaching it to the response.

raw_tools.name: type_text
raw_tools.description: Type text using keyboard into a previously focused input

text.description: The text to type

submitKey.description: Optional key to press after typing. E.g., "Enter", "Tab", "Escape"

raw_tools.name: upload_file
raw_tools.description: Upload a file through a provided element.

uid.description: The uid of the file input element or an element that will open file chooser on the page from the page content snapshot

filePath.description: The local path of the file to upload

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

raw_tools.name: wait_for
raw_tools.description: Wait for the specified text to appear on the selected page.

text.description: Non-empty list of texts. Resolves when any value appears on the page.

timeout.description: Maximum wait time in milliseconds. If set to 0, the default timeout will be used.

raw_tools.name: click
raw_tools.description: Clicks on the provided element

uid.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot

dblClick.description: Set to true for double clicks. Default is false.

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

raw_tools.name: close_page
raw_tools.description: Closes the page by its index. The last open page cannot be closed.

pageId.description: The ID of the page to close. Call list_pages to list pages.

raw_tools.name: drag
raw_tools.description: Drag an element onto another element

from_uid.description: The uid of the element to drag

to_uid.description: The uid of the element to drop into

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

raw_tools.name: emulate
raw_tools.description: Emulates various features on the selected page.

networkConditions.description: Throttle network. Set to "No emulation" to disable. If omitted, conditions remain unchanged.

cpuThrottlingRate.description: Represents the CPU slowdown factor. Set the rate to 1 to disable throttling. If omitted, throttling remains unchanged.

latitude.description: Latitude between -90 and 90.

longitude.description: Longitude between -180 and 180.

geolocation.description: Geolocation to emulate. Set to null to clear the geolocation override.

userAgent.description: User agent to emulate. Set to null to clear the user agent override.

colorScheme.description: Emulate the dark or the light mode. Set to "auto" to reset to the default.

width.description: Page width in pixels.

height.description: Page height in pixels.

deviceScaleFactor.description: Specify device scale factor (can be thought of as dpr).

isMobile.description: Whether the meta viewport tag is taken into account. Defaults to false.

hasTouch.description: Specifies if viewport supports touch events. This should be set to true for mobile devices.

isLandscape.description: Specifies if viewport is in landscape mode. Defaults to false.

viewport.description: Viewport to emulate. Set to null to reset to the default viewport.

raw_tools.name: evaluate_script
raw_tools.description:
Evaluate a JavaScript function inside the currently selected page. Returns the response as JSON,
so returned values have to be JSON-serializable.

uid.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot

args.description: An optional list of arguments to pass to the function.

raw_tools.name: fill
raw_tools.description: Type text into a input, text area or select an option from a <select> element.

uid.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

raw_tools.name: fill_form
raw_tools.description: Fill out multiple form elements at once

uid.description: The uid of the element to fill out

elements.description: Elements from snapshot to fill out.

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

raw_tools.name: get_console_message
raw_tools.description: Gets a console message by its ID. You can get all messages by calling list_console_messages.

msgid.description: The msgid of a console message on the page from the listed console messages

raw_tools.name: get_network_request
raw_tools.description: Gets a network request by an optional reqid, if omitted returns the currently selected request in the DevTools Network panel.

reqid.description: The reqid of the network request. If omitted returns the currently selected request in the DevTools Network panel.

requestFilePath.description: The absolute or relative path to save the request body to. If omitted, the body is returned inline.

responseFilePath.description: The absolute or relative path to save the response body to. If omitted, the body is returned inline.

raw_tools.name: handle_dialog
raw_tools.description: If a browser dialog was opened, use this command to handle it

action.description: Whether to dismiss or accept the dialog

promptText.description: Optional prompt text to enter into the dialog.

raw_tools.name: hover
raw_tools.description: Hover over the provided element

uid.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

raw_tools.name: list_console_messages
raw_tools.description: List all console messages for the currently selected page since the last navigation.

pageSize.description: Maximum number of messages to return. When omitted, returns all requests.

pageIdx.description: Page number to return (0-based). When omitted, returns the first page.

types.description: Filter messages to only return messages of the specified resource types. When omitted or empty, returns all messages.

includePreservedMessages.description: Set to true to return the preserved messages over the last 3 navigations.

raw_tools.name: list_network_requests
raw_tools.description: List all requests for the currently selected page since the last navigation.

pageSize.description: Maximum number of requests to return. When omitted, returns all requests.

pageIdx.description: Page number to return (0-based). When omitted, returns the first page.

resourceTypes.description: Filter requests to only return requests of the specified resource types. When omitted or empty, returns all requests.

includePreservedRequests.description: Set to true to return the preserved requests over the last 3 navigations.

raw_tools.name: list_pages
raw_tools.description: Get a list of pages  open in the browser.

raw_tools.name: navigate_page
raw_tools.description: Navigates the currently selected page to a URL.

type.description: Navigate the page by URL, back or forward in history, or reload.

url.description: Target URL (only type=url)

ignoreCache.description: Whether to ignore cache on reload.

handleBeforeUnload.description: Whether to auto accept or beforeunload dialogs triggered by this navigation. Default is accept.

initScript.description: A JavaScript script to be executed on each new document before any other scripts for the next navigation.

timeout.description: Maximum wait time in milliseconds. If set to 0, the default timeout will be used.

raw_tools.name: new_page
raw_tools.description: Creates a new page

url.description: URL to load in a new page.

background.description: Whether to open the page in the background without bringing it to the front. Default is false (foreground).

isolatedContext.description: If specified, the page is created in an isolated browser context with the given name. Pages in the same browser context share cookies and storage. Pages in different browser contexts are fully isolated.

timeout.description: Maximum wait time in milliseconds. If set to 0, the default timeout will be used.

raw_tools.name: performance_analyze_insight
raw_tools.description: Provides more detailed information on a specific Performance Insight of an insight set that was highlighted in the results of a trace recording.

insightSetId.description: The id for the specific insight set. Only use the ids given in the "Available insight sets" list.

insightName.description: The name of the Insight you want more information on. For example: "DocumentLatency" or "LCPBreakdown"

raw_tools.name: performance_start_trace
raw_tools.description: Starts a performance trace recording on the selected page. This can be used to look for performance problems and insights to improve the performance of the page. It will also report Core Web Vital (CWV) scores for the page.

reload.description: Determines if, once tracing has started, the current selected page should be automatically reloaded. Navigate the page to the right URL using the navigate_page tool BEFORE starting the trace if reload or autoStop is set to true.

autoStop.description: Determines if the trace recording should be automatically stopped.

filePath.description: The absolute file path, or a file path relative to the current working directory, to save the raw trace data. For example, trace.json.gz (compressed) or trace.json (uncompressed).

raw_tools.name: performance_stop_trace
raw_tools.description: Stops the active performance trace recording on the selected page.

filePath.description: The absolute file path, or a file path relative to the current working directory, to save the raw trace data. For example, trace.json.gz (compressed) or trace.json (uncompressed).

raw_tools.name: press_key
raw_tools.description: Press a key or key combination. Use this when other input methods like fill() cannot be used (e.g., keyboard shortcuts, navigation keys, or special key combinations).

key.description: A key or a combination (e.g., "Enter", "Control+A", "Control++", "Control+Shift+R"). Modifiers: Control, Shift, Alt, Meta

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

raw_tools.name: resize_page
raw_tools.description: Resizes the selected page's window so that the page has specified dimension

width.description: Page width

height.description: Page height

raw_tools.description: Lists all available library documentation from Context7. The library names can be used with 'get-library-documentation' to retrieve documentation.

raw_tools.name: resolve-library-id
raw_tools.description:
Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns a list of matching libraries.

You MUST call this function before 'get-library-docs' to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Selection Process:
1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for
2. Return the most relevant match based on:
- Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
- Description relevance to the query's intent
- Documentation coverage (prioritize libraries with higher Code Snippet counts)
- Trust score (consider libraries with scores of 7-10 more authoritative)

Response Format:
- Return the selected library ID in a clearly marked section
- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen
- If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
- If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements

For ambiguous queries, request clarification before proceeding with a best-guess match.

- Description relevance to the query's intent

- Source reputation (consider libraries with High or Medium reputation more authoritative)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)

- Return the selected library ID in a clearly marked section
- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen
- If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
- If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements

For ambiguous queries, request clarification before proceeding with a best-guess match.

raw_tools.name: API-update-page-markdown
raw_tools.description:
Notion | Update a page's content as Markdown
Error Responses:
400: Bad request
403: The integration lacks the read/update content capability required for this page.
404: Page not found or not shared with the integration.
409: Conflict (e.g. row limit exceeded).
429: Rate limited.

page_id.description: Identifier for a Notion page (or block) to read or update as markdown.

type.description: The kind of edit to apply. Prefer `replace_content` (overwrite the whole page) or `update_content` (targeted find-and-replace). `insert_content` and `replace_content_range` are deprecated.

anyOf.description: Provide when type is `replace_content`. Replaces the entire page content.

new_str.description: The complete new page content as enhanced Markdown.

allow_deleting_content.description: Permit deletion of existing child pages/databases that are no longer present in the new content.

anyOf.description: Provide when type is `update_content`. Applies targeted find-and-replace edits.

content_updates.description: Up to 100 find-and-replace edits applied in order.

old_str.description: Exact existing Markdown text to find.

replace_all_matches.description: Replace every occurrence of old_str instead of just the first (default false).

allow_deleting_content.description: Permit deletion of existing child pages/databases removed by the edits.

anyOf.description: Deprecated. Provide when type is `insert_content`. Inserts Markdown at a position.

after.description: Ellipsis-format selection ("start text...end text") to insert after. Cannot be combined with position.

position.description: Insert at the start or end of the page. Cannot be combined with after.

anyOf.description: Deprecated. Provide when type is `replace_content_range`. Replaces a selected range of Markdown.

content.description: New Markdown content for the range.

content_range.description: Ellipsis-format selection ("start text...end text") identifying the range to replace.

allow_deleting_content.description: Permit deletion of child pages/databases within the replaced range.

raw_tools.name: billing_getCatalogItemListV1
raw_tools.description:
This endpoint retrieves a list of catalog items available for order. 

Prices in catalog items is displayed as cents (without floating point), e.g: float `17.99` is displayed as integer `1799`.

name.description: Filter catalog items by name. Use `*` for wildcard search, e.g. `.COM*` to find .com domain

raw_tools.name: billing_createNewServiceOrderV1
raw_tools.description:
This endpoint creates a new service order. 

To place order, you need to provide payment method ID and list of price items from the catalog endpoint together with quantity.
Coupons also can be provided during order creation.

Orders created using this endpoint will be set for automatic renewal.

Some `credit_card` payments might need additional verification, rendering purchase unprocessed.
We recommend use other payment methods than `credit_card` if you encounter this issue.

payment_method_id.description: Payment method ID

raw_tools.name: billing_setDefaultPaymentMethodV1
raw_tools.description: This endpoint sets default payment method for your account.

raw_tools.name: billing_deletePaymentMethodV1
raw_tools.description: This endpoint deletes a payment method from your account.

raw_tools.name: billing_getPaymentMethodListV1
raw_tools.description:
This endpoint retrieves a list of available payment methods that can be used for placing new orders.

If you want to add new payment method, please use [hPanel](https://hpanel.hostinger.com/billing/payment-methods).

raw_tools.name: billing_cancelSubscriptionV1
raw_tools.description: This endpoint cancels a subscription and stops any further billing.

raw_tools.name: billing_getSubscriptionListV1
raw_tools.description: This endpoint retrieves a list of all subscriptions associated with your account.

raw_tools.name: DNS_getSnapshotV1
raw_tools.description: This endpoint retrieves particular DNS snapshot with the contents of DNS zone records.

raw_tools.name: DNS_getSnapshotListV1
raw_tools.description: This endpoint retrieves list of DNS snapshots.

raw_tools.name: DNS_restoreSnapshotV1
raw_tools.description: This endpoint restores DNS zone to the selected snapshot.

raw_tools.name: DNS_getRecordsV1
raw_tools.description: This endpoint retrieves DNS zone records for a specific domain.

raw_tools.name: DNS_updateZoneRecordsV1
raw_tools.description:
This endpoint updates DNS records for the selected domain. 

Using `overwrite = true` will replace existing records with the provided ones. 
Otherwise existing records will be updated and new records will be added.

overwrite.description: If `true`, resource records (RRs) matching name and type will be deleted and new RRs will be created, otherwise resource records' ttl's are updated and new records are appended. If no matching RRs are found, they are created.

name.description: Name of the record (use `@` for wildcard name)

type.description: Type of the record

raw_tools.name: DNS_deleteZoneRecordsV1
raw_tools.description:
This endpoint deletes DNS records for the selected domain. 
To filter which records to delete, add the `name` of the record and `type` to the filter. 
Multiple filters can be provided with single request.

If you have multiple records with the same name and type, and you want to delete only part of them,
refer to the `Update zone records` endpoint.

raw_tools.name: DNS_resetZoneRecordsV1
raw_tools.description: This endpoint resets DNS zone to the default records.

sync.description: Determines if operation should be run synchronously

reset_email_records.description: Determines if email records should be reset

whitelisted_record_types.description: Specifies which record types to not reset

raw_tools.name: DNS_validateZoneRecordsV1
raw_tools.description:
This endpoint used to validate DNS records prior update for the selected domain. 

If the validation is successful, the response will contain `200 Success` code.
If there is validation error, the response will fail with `422 Validation error` code.

overwrite.description: If `true`, resource records (RRs) matching name and type will be deleted and new RRs will be created, otherwise resource records' ttl's are updated and new records are appended. If no matching RRs are found, they are created.

name.description: Name of the record (use `@` for wildcard name)

type.description: Type of the record

raw_tools.name: domains_checkDomainAvailabilityV1

Recovery mode is a special state that allows users to perform system rescue operations, 
such as repairing file systems, recovering data, or troubleshooting issues that prevent the virtual machine 
from booting normally. 

Virtual machine will boot recovery disk image and original disk image will be mounted in `/mnt` directory.

root_password.description: Temporary root password for recovery mode

raw_tools.name: VPS_stopRecoveryModeV1
raw_tools.description:

If virtual machine is not in recovery mode, this operation will fail.

raw_tools.name: VPS_recreateVirtualMachineV1
raw_tools.description:
This endpoint will recreate a virtual machine from scratch. 
The recreation process involves reinstalling the operating system and resetting the virtual machine to its initial state.
Snapshots, if there are any, will be deleted.

## Password Requirements
Password will be checked against leaked password databases. 
Requirements for the password are:
- At least 8 characters long
- At least one uppercase letter
- At least one lowercase letter
- At least one number
- Is not leaked publicly

**This operation is irreversible and will result in the loss of all data stored on the virtual machine!**

password.description: Password for the virtual machine. If not provided, random password will be generated. Password will not be shown in the response.

raw_tools.name: VPS_restartVirtualMachineV1

If the virtual machine was stopped, it will be started.

allowing users to restore the virtual machine to that state if needed.

The recreation process involves reinstalling the operating system and resetting the virtual machine to its initial state.
Snapshots, if there are any, will be deleted.

## Password Requirements
Password will be checked against leaked password databases. 
Requirements for the password are:
- At least 8 characters long
- At least one uppercase letter
- At least one lowercase letter
- At least one number
- Is not leaked publicly

**This operation is irreversible and will result in the loss of all data stored on the virtual machine!**

Use this endpoint to completely rebuild VPS instances with fresh OS installation.

associated resources including networks, volumes, and images.

projectName.description: Docker Compose project name using alphanumeric characters, dashes, and underscores only

raw_tools.name: VPS_getProjectListV1
raw_tools.description:
Retrieves a list of all Docker Compose projects currently deployed on the virtual machine. 

This endpoint returns basic information about each project including name, status, file path and list of containers with 
details about their names, image, status, health and ports. Container stats are omitted in this endpoint.
If you need to get detailed information about container with stats included, use the `Get project containers` endpoint.

The response contains the last 300 log entries across all services.

projectName.description: Docker Compose project name using alphanumeric characters, dashes, and underscores only

raw_tools.name: VPS_startProjectV1
raw_tools.description:

This operation brings up containers in the correct dependency order as defined in the compose file.

projectName.description: Docker Compose project name using alphanumeric characters, dashes, and underscores only

raw_tools.name: VPS_stopProjectV1
raw_tools.description:
Stops all running services in a Docker Compose project while preserving container configurations and data volumes.

Use this to temporarily halt a project without removing data or configurations.

projectName.description: Docker Compose project name using alphanumeric characters, dashes, and underscores only

raw_tools.name: VPS_updateProjectV1
raw_tools.description:
Updates a Docker Compose project by pulling the latest image versions and recreating containers with new configurations. 

This operation preserves data volumes while applying changes from the compose file. 

Use this to deploy application updates, apply configuration changes, or refresh container images to their latest versions.

projectName.description: Docker Compose project name using alphanumeric characters, dashes, and underscores only

such as repairing file systems, recovering data, or troubleshooting issues that prevent the virtual machine 
from booting normally. 

Virtual machine will boot recovery disk image and original disk image will be mounted in `/mnt` directory.

Use this endpoint to enable system rescue operations on VPS instances.

root_password.description: Temporary root password for recovery mode

raw_tools.name: VPS_stopRecoveryModeV1
raw_tools.description:
Stop recovery mode for a specified virtual machine.

If virtual machine is not in recovery mode, this operation will fail.

Use this endpoint to exit system rescue mode and return VPS to normal operation.

raw_tools.name: VPS_recreateVirtualMachineV1
raw_tools.description:
Recreate a virtual machine from scratch.

The recreation process involves reinstalling the operating system and resetting the virtual machine to its initial state.
Snapshots, if there are any, will be deleted.

## Password Requirements
Password will be checked against leaked password databases. 
Requirements for the password are:
- At least 12 characters long
- At least one uppercase letter
- At least one lowercase letter
- At least one number
- Is not leaked publicly

**This operation is irreversible and will result in the loss of all data stored on the virtual machine!**

Use this endpoint to completely rebuild VPS instances with fresh OS installation.

password.description: Root password for the virtual machine. If not provided, random password will be generated. Password will not be shown in the response.

panel_password.description: Panel password for the panel-based OS template. If not provided, random password will be generated. If OS does not support panel_password this field will be ignored. Password will not be shown in the response.

post_install_script_id.description: Post-install script to execute after virtual machine was recreated

allowing users to restore the virtual machine to that state if needed. 
This operation is useful for backup purposes, system recovery, 
and testing changes without affecting the current state of the virtual machine.

raw_tools.name: hosting_importWordpressWebsite
raw_tools.description: Import a WordPress website from an archive file to a hosting server. This tool uploads a website archive (zip, tar, tar.gz, etc.) and a database dump (.sql file) to deploy a complete WordPress website. The archive will be extracted on the server automatically. Note: This process may take a while for larger sites. After upload completion, files are being extracted and the site will be available in a few minutes. The username will be automatically resolved from the domain.

domain.description: Domain name associated with the hosting account (e.g., example.com)

If user provides directory path, create archive from it before proceeding using EXACTLY this naming pattern: directoryname_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.zip (e.g., mywebsite_20250115_143022.zip)

databaseDump.description: Absolute or relative path to a database dump file (.sql)

domain.description: Domain name associated with the hosting account (e.g., example.com)

archivePath.description: Absolute or relative path to the application archive file. Supported formats: zip, tar, tar.gz, tgz, 7z, gz, gzip. If user provides directory path, create archive from it before proceeding. IMPORTANT: the archive must ONLY contain application source files, not the build output, skip node_modules directory.

raw_tools.name: hosting_createNodeJSBuildFromArchiveV1
raw_tools.description:
Upload a project archive, auto-detect build settings, and immediately start a Node.js build.

This is the recommended single-step approach for deploying a Node.js application.
The archive is uploaded to the website's file storage, build settings are auto-detected
from the package.json inside the archive, and the build process starts automatically.
Optional override fields take precedence over auto-detected values.
Maximum archive size is 50MB.

Before archiving, exclude `node_modules/` and any build output directories
(e.g. `dist/`, `.next/`, `build/`) — they are not needed because the build
process runs the install step automatically, and including them unnecessarily
increases the archive size. This also helps keep the archive well under the 50MB limit.

Example (zip):
```
zip -r archive.zip . --exclude "node_modules/*" --exclude "dist/*"
```

The returned build `uuid` can be used to poll progress and retrieve logs via
the `Get Node.js Build Logs` endpoint.

Call GET /api/hosting/v1/wordpress/installations filtered by username and

(the default), the async job will fail.

job has been queued, not that WordPress is ready. Installation typically
takes 1-2 minutes. Poll GET /api/hosting/v1/wordpress/installations filtered
by username and domain to track progress. When the installation appears in

Retrieve detailed information about a specified virtual machine.

Use this endpoint to view comprehensive VPS configuration and status.

raw_tools.name: VPS_getVirtualMachinesV1
raw_tools.description:
Retrieve all available virtual machines.

Use this endpoint to view available VPS instances.

raw_tools.name: VPS_purchaseNewVirtualMachineV1
raw_tools.description:
Purchase and setup a new virtual machine.

If virtual machine setup fails for any reason, login to
[hPanel](https://hpanel.hostinger.com/) and complete the setup manually.

If no payment method is provided, your default payment method will be used automatically.

Use this endpoint to create new VPS instances.

raw_tools.name: VPS_getScanMetricsV1
raw_tools.description:
Retrieve scan metrics for the [Monarx](https://www.monarx.com/) malware scanner
installed on a specified virtual machine.

The scan metrics provide detailed information about malware scans performed
by Monarx, including number of scans, detected threats, and other relevant
statistics. This information is useful for monitoring security status of the
virtual machine and assessing effectiveness of the malware scanner.

Use this endpoint to monitor VPS security scan results and threat detection.

raw_tools.name: VPS_installMonarxV1
raw_tools.description:
Install the Monarx malware scanner on a specified virtual machine.

[Monarx](https://www.monarx.com/) is a security tool designed to detect and
prevent malware infections on virtual machines. By installing Monarx, users
can enhance the security of their virtual machines, ensuring that they are
protected against malicious software.

Use this endpoint to enable malware protection on VPS instances.

raw_tools.name: VPS_uninstallMonarxV1
raw_tools.description:
Uninstall the Monarx malware scanner on a specified virtual machine.

If Monarx is not installed, the request will still be processed without any effect.

Use this endpoint to remove malware scanner from VPS instances.

raw_tools.name: VPS_getMetricsV1
raw_tools.description:
Retrieve historical metrics for a specified virtual machine.

It includes the following metrics: 
- CPU usage
- Memory usage
- Disk usage
- Network usage
- Uptime

Use this endpoint to monitor VPS performance and resource utilization over time.

raw_tools.name: VPS_setNameserversV1
raw_tools.description:
Set nameservers for a specified virtual machine.

Be aware, that improper nameserver configuration can lead to the virtual
machine being unable to resolve domain names.

Use this endpoint to configure custom DNS resolvers for VPS instances.

raw_tools.name: VPS_createPTRRecordV1
raw_tools.description:
Create or update a PTR (Pointer) record for a specified virtual machine.

Use this endpoint to configure reverse DNS lookup for VPS IP addresses.

raw_tools.name: VPS_deletePTRRecordV1
raw_tools.description:
Delete a PTR (Pointer) record for a specified virtual machine.

Once deleted, reverse DNS lookups to the virtual machine's IP address will
no longer return the previously configured hostname.

Use this endpoint to remove reverse DNS configuration from VPS instances.

raw_tools.name: VPS_setPanelPasswordV1
raw_tools.description:
Set panel password for a specified virtual machine.

If virtual machine does not use panel OS, the request will still be processed without any effect.
Requirements for password are same as in the [recreate virtual machine
endpoint](/#tag/vps-virtual-machine/POST/api/vps/v1/virtual-machines/{virtualMachineId}/recreate).

Use this endpoint to configure control panel access credentials for VPS instances.

password.description: Panel password for the virtual machine

raw_tools.name: VPS_startRecoveryModeV1
raw_tools.description:
Initiate recovery mode for a specified virtual machine.

Recovery mode is a special state that allows users to perform system rescue operations, 
such as repairing file systems, recovering data, or troubleshooting issues that prevent the virtual machine 
from booting normally. 

Virtual machine will boot recovery disk image and original disk image will be mounted in `/mnt` directory.

Use this endpoint to enable system rescue operations on VPS instances.

root_password.description: Temporary root password for recovery mode

raw_tools.name: VPS_stopRecoveryModeV1
raw_tools.description:
Stop recovery mode for a specified virtual machine.

If virtual machine is not in recovery mode, this operation will fail.

Use this endpoint to exit system rescue mode and return VPS to normal operation.

raw_tools.name: VPS_recreateVirtualMachineV1
raw_tools.description:
Recreate a virtual machine from scratch.

The recreation process involves reinstalling the operating system and
resetting the virtual machine to its initial state.
Snapshots, if there are any, will be deleted.

## Password Requirements
Password will be checked against leaked password databases. 
Requirements for the password are:
- At least 12 characters long
- At least one uppercase letter
- At least one lowercase letter
- At least one number
- Is not leaked publicly

**This operation is irreversible and will result in the loss of all data stored on the virtual machine!**

Use this endpoint to completely rebuild VPS instances with fresh OS installation.

password.description:
Root password for the virtual machine. If not provided, random password will be generated.
Password will not be shown in the response.

panel_password.description:
Panel password for the panel-based OS template. If not provided, random password will be generated.
If OS does not support panel_password this field will be ignored.
Password will not be shown in the response.

post_install_script_id.description: Post-install script to execute after virtual machine was recreated

raw_tools.name: VPS_restartVirtualMachineV1
raw_tools.description:
Restart a specified virtual machine by fully stopping and starting it.

If the virtual machine was stopped, it will be started.

Use this endpoint to reboot VPS instances.

raw_tools.name: VPS_setRootPasswordV1
raw_tools.description:
Set root password for a specified virtual machine.

Requirements for password are same as in the [recreate virtual machine
endpoint](/#tag/vps-virtual-machine/POST/api/vps/v1/virtual-machines/{virtualMachineId}/recreate).

Use this endpoint to update administrator credentials for VPS instances.

password.description: Root password for the virtual machine

raw_tools.name: VPS_setupPurchasedVirtualMachineV1
raw_tools.description:
Setup newly purchased virtual machine with `initial` state.

Use this endpoint to configure and initialize purchased VPS instances.

Password will not be shown in the response.

hostname.description: Override default hostname of the virtual machine

name.description: Name of the SSH key

raw_tools.name: VPS_getSnapshotV1
raw_tools.description:
Retrieve snapshot for a specified virtual machine.

Use this endpoint to view current VPS snapshot information.

raw_tools.name: VPS_createSnapshotV1
raw_tools.description:
Create a snapshot of a specified virtual machine.

A snapshot captures the state and data of the virtual machine at a specific point in time, 
allowing users to restore the virtual machine to that state if needed. 
This operation is useful for backup purposes, system recovery, 
and testing changes without affecting the current state of the virtual machine.

**Creating new snapshot will overwrite the existing snapshot!**

Use this endpoint to capture VPS state for backup and recovery purposes.

raw_tools.name: VPS_deleteSnapshotV1
raw_tools.description:
Delete a snapshot of a specified virtual machine.

Use this endpoint to remove VPS snapshots.

raw_tools.name: VPS_restoreSnapshotV1
raw_tools.description:
Restore a specified virtual machine to a previous state using a snapshot.

Restoring from a snapshot allows users to revert the virtual machine to that state,
which is useful for system recovery, undoing changes, or testing.

Use this endpoint to revert VPS instances to previous saved states.

raw_tools.name: VPS_startVirtualMachineV1
raw_tools.description:
Start a specified virtual machine.

If the virtual machine is already running, the request will still be processed without any effect.

Use this endpoint to power on stopped VPS instances.

raw_tools.name: VPS_stopVirtualMachineV1
raw_tools.description:
Stop a specified virtual machine.

If the virtual machine is already stopped, the request will still be processed without any effect.

Use this endpoint to power off running VPS instances.

raw_tools.name: hosting_importWordpressWebsite

states.description: Build states to filter by

raw_tools.name: hosting_createNodeJSBuildFromArchiveV1
raw_tools.description:
Upload a project archive, auto-detect build settings, and immediately start a Node.js build.

This is the recommended single-step approach for deploying a Node.js application.
The archive is uploaded to the website's file storage, build settings are auto-detected
from the package.json inside the archive, and the build process starts automatically.
Optional override fields take precedence over auto-detected values.
Maximum archive size is 50MB.

Before archiving, exclude `node_modules/` and any build output directories
(e.g. `dist/`, `.next/`, `build/`) — they are not needed because the build
process runs the install step automatically, and including them unnecessarily
increases the archive size. This also helps keep the archive well under the 50MB limit.

Example (zip):
```
zip -r archive.zip . --exclude "node_modules/*" --exclude "dist/*"
```

The returned build `uuid` can be used to poll progress and retrieve logs via
the `Get Node.js Build Logs` endpoint.

node_version.description: Node.js version override (auto-detected from package.json if omitted)

root_directory.description: Application root directory override (where package.json is located) relative to public_html

output_directory.description: Build output directory override relative to the root directory

raw_tools.name: hosting_getNodeJSBuildLogsV1
raw_tools.description:
Retrieve logs from a specific Node.js build process.

To stream live output while a build is running, poll this endpoint repeatedly
while the build state is `running`, passing the previously returned `lines` count
as `from_line` to fetch only new output since the last call.
Log content may contain ANSI escape sequences (color codes).

from_line.description: Line from which to start retrieving logs

raw_tools.name: hosting_installWordPressV1
raw_tools.description:
Install WordPress on an existing website.

The website must already exist before calling this endpoint. To create a new
website first, use POST /api/hosting/v1/websites and poll
GET /api/hosting/v1/websites until it appears.

Call GET /api/hosting/v1/wordpress/installations filtered by username and
domain before proceeding to check whether WordPress is already installed on
the target domain/path. If WordPress already exists and `overwrite` is false
(the default), the async job will fail.

This operation is asynchronous: a successful response only means the install
job has been queued, not that WordPress is ready. Installation typically
takes 1-2 minutes. Poll GET /api/hosting/v1/wordpress/installations filtered
by username and domain to track progress. When the installation appears in
that list, WordPress is ready.

domain.description: Domain of the existing website where WordPress will be installed

language.description: WordPress locale. Defaults to en_US when omitted.

directory.description: Relative directory to install WordPress into. Defaults to the website root when omitted.

overwrite.description: When false (default), does not replace an existing installation. If WordPress is already installed on the domain/path, the async install job fails unless true.

version.description: WordPress core version to install. If omitted, the latest core version compatible with the account vhost PHP version is selected.

password.description: password parameter

database.description: Optional. If the named database already exists, it will be used for this WordPress install. Otherwise a new database is created with a generated name and random credentials.

name.description: Database name (username prefix added if missing)

password.description: password parameter

Each installation includes a `valid` flag and, when invalid, a
`validationError` describing why.

ownership.description: Filter by ownership type. Defaults to "owned". Use "all" to include both owned and managed installations.

raw_tools.name: VPS_recreateVirtualMachineV1
raw_tools.description:
Recreate a virtual machine from scratch.

The recreation process involves reinstalling the operating system and
resetting the virtual machine to its initial state.
Snapshots, if there are any, will be deleted.

## Password Requirements
Password will be checked against leaked password databases. 
Requirements for the password are:
- At least 12 characters long
- At least one uppercase letter
- At least one lowercase letter
- At least one number
- Is not leaked publicly

**This operation is irreversible and will result in the loss of all data stored on the virtual machine!**

Use this endpoint to completely rebuild VPS instances with fresh OS installation.

password.description:
Root password for the virtual machine. If not provided, random password will be generated.
Password will not be shown in the response.

panel_password.description:
Panel password for the panel-based OS template. If not provided, random password will be generated.
If OS does not support panel_password this field will be ignored.
Password will not be shown in the response.

raw_tools.name: horizons_createWebsiteV1
raw_tools.description:
Create new Hostinger Horizons website from the given message.\n
Use this tool when user asks you to create a website, landing page, blog
or any other type of application.\n
This tool initiates the website creation process and returns a website URL and ID.
The generation happens asynchronously.\n
After invoking this tool, your chat reply must be EXACTLY 1 sentence summarizing
that Hostinger Horizons is now creating their website and it will be ready in a few minutes
and you should provide the website URL to the user immediately
Do not write code.\n\nTo edit afterwards, users must go to Hostinger Horizons interface
in the provided website URL.
If the tool call fails with an error, you should provide a clear explanation of the error
and do not generate code yourself in the chat.
\n
TECHNOLOGY STACK CONSTRAINTS (STRICTLY ENFORCED):\n
The environment is limited to the following technologies.
You MUST NOT use, suggest, or implement any technology outside this list:\n
\n
- Language: JavaScript ONLY.
- Languages like TypeScript, Rust, Python, Java, PHP, etc., are STRICTLY PROHIBITED.\n
- Framework: React.\n
- Navigation: React Router.\n
- Styling: TailwindCSS.\n
- Components: shadcn/ui (built with @radix-ui primitives).\n
- Icons: Lucide React.\n
- Animations: Framer Motion.\n
\n
BACKEND & DATA STORAGE:\n
- Horizons integrated backend is the EXCLUSIVE solution for persistent data storage,
authentication, and database needs.\n
- Local databases (SQLite, MySQL, etc.) are STRICTLY PROHIBITED.\n
- Third-party services (Firebase, AWS Amplify) are allowed ONLY if explicitly requested by the user.\n
\n
MAPS:\n
- OpenStreetMap is the default provider.\n
- Alternative providers (Google Maps, Mapbox) are allowed ONLY if explicitly requested by the user.\n

type.description: type parameter

text.description:
Detailed project specification.
Include purpose, key features, user flows, data models, and design preferences.
The specification should be detailed and comprehensive, covering all aspects of the project.

raw_tools.name: hosting_createNodeJSBuildFromArchiveV1
raw_tools.description:
Upload a project archive, auto-detect build settings, and immediately start a Node.js build.

This is the recommended single-step approach for deploying a Node.js application.
The archive is uploaded to the website's file storage, build settings are auto-detected
from the package.json inside the archive, and the build process starts automatically.
Optional override fields take precedence over auto-detected values.
Maximum archive size is 50MB.

Before archiving, exclude `node_modules/` and any build output directories
(e.g. `dist/`, `.next/`, `build/`) — they are not needed because the build
process runs the install step automatically, and including them unnecessarily
increases the archive size. This also helps keep the archive well under the 50MB limit.

Example (zip):
```
zip -r archive.zip . --exclude "node_modules/*" --exclude "dist/*"
```

The returned build `uuid` can be used to poll progress and retrieve logs via
the `Get Node.js Build Logs` endpoint.

node_version.description: Node.js version override (auto-detected from package.json if omitted)

root_directory.description: Application root directory override (where package.json is located) relative to public_html

output_directory.description: Build output directory override relative to the root directory

and do not generate code yourself in the chat.

TECHNOLOGY STACK CONSTRAINTS (STRICTLY ENFORCED):\n
The environment is limited to the following technologies.
You MUST NOT use, suggest, or implement any technology outside this list:\n

- Language: JavaScript ONLY.

- Framework: React.\n

- Styling: TailwindCSS.\n
- Components: shadcn/ui (built with @radix-ui primitives).\n
- Icons: Lucide React.\n
- Animations: Framer Motion.\n
\n
BACKEND & DATA STORAGE:\n
- Horizons integrated backend is the EXCLUSIVE solution for persistent data storage,
authentication, and database needs.\n
- Local databases (SQLite, MySQL, etc.) are STRICTLY PROHIBITED.\n
- Third-party services (Firebase, AWS Amplify) are allowed ONLY if explicitly requested by the user.\n
\n
MAPS:\n

from the package.json inside the archive, and the build process starts automatically.
Optional override fields take precedence over auto-detected values.

(e.g. `dist/`, `.next/`, `build/`) — they are not needed because the build
process runs the install step automatically, and including them unnecessarily
increases the archive size. This also helps keep the archive well under the 50MB limit.

Example (zip):
```
zip -r archive.zip . --exclude "node_modules/*" --exclude "dist/*"
```

The returned build `uuid` can be used to poll progress and retrieve logs via
the `Get Node.js Build Logs` endpoint.

raw_tools.name: VPS_recreateVirtualMachineV1
raw_tools.description:
Recreate a virtual machine from scratch.

The recreation process involves reinstalling the operating system and
resetting the virtual machine to its initial state.
Snapshots, if there are any, will be deleted.

## Password Requirements
Password will be checked against leaked password databases. 
Requirements for the password are:
- At least 12 characters long
- At least one uppercase letter
- At least one lowercase letter
- At least one number
- Is not leaked publicly

**This operation is irreversible and will result in the loss of all data stored on the virtual machine!**

Use this endpoint to completely rebuild VPS instances with fresh OS installation.

password.description:
Root password for the virtual machine. If not provided, random password will be generated.
Password will not be shown in the response.

panel_password.description:
Panel password for the panel-based OS template. If not provided, random password will be generated.
If OS does not support panel_password this field will be ignored.
Password will not be shown in the response.

raw_tools.name: hosting_installWordPressV1
raw_tools.description:
Install WordPress on an existing website.

The website must already exist before calling this endpoint. To create a new
website first, use POST /api/hosting/v1/websites and poll
GET /api/hosting/v1/websites until it appears.

Call GET /api/hosting/v1/wordpress/installations filtered by username and
domain before proceeding to check whether WordPress is already installed on
the target domain/path. If WordPress already exists and `overwrite` is false
(the default), the async job will fail.

This operation is asynchronous: a successful response only means the install
job has been queued, not that WordPress is ready. Installation typically
takes 1-2 minutes. Poll GET /api/hosting/v1/wordpress/installations filtered
by username and domain to track progress. When the installation appears in
that list, WordPress is ready.

domain.description: Domain of the existing website where WordPress will be installed

language.description: WordPress locale. Defaults to en_US when omitted.

directory.description: Relative directory to install WordPress into. Defaults to the website root when omitted.

overwrite.description: When false (default), does not replace an existing installation. If WordPress is already installed on the domain/path, the async install job fails unless true.

version.description: WordPress core version to install. If omitted, the latest core version compatible with the account vhost PHP version is selected.

password.description: password parameter

database.description: Optional. If the named database already exists, it will be used for this WordPress install. Otherwise a new database is created with a generated name and random credentials.

name.description: Database name (username prefix added if missing)

password.description: password parameter

The generation happens asynchronously.\n
After invoking this tool, your chat reply must be EXACTLY 1 sentence summarizing
that Hostinger Horizons is now creating their website and it will be ready in a few minutes
and you should provide the website URL to the user immediately
Do not write code.\n\nTo edit afterwards, users must go to Hostinger Horizons interface
in the provided website URL.

and do not generate code yourself in the chat.
\n
TECHNOLOGY STACK CONSTRAINTS (STRICTLY ENFORCED):\n
The environment is limited to the following technologies.
You MUST NOT use, suggest, or implement any technology outside this list:\n
\n
- Language: JavaScript ONLY.
- Languages like TypeScript, Rust, Python, Java, PHP, etc., are STRICTLY PROHIBITED.\n
- Framework: React.\n
- Navigation: React Router.\n
- Styling: TailwindCSS.\n
- Components: shadcn/ui (built with @radix-ui primitives).\n
- Icons: Lucide React.\n
- Animations: Framer Motion.\n
\n
BACKEND & DATA STORAGE:\n
- Horizons integrated backend is the EXCLUSIVE solution for persistent data storage,
authentication, and database needs.\n
- Local databases (SQLite, MySQL, etc.) are STRICTLY PROHIBITED.\n
- Third-party services (Firebase, AWS Amplify) are allowed ONLY if explicitly requested by the user.\n
\n
MAPS:\n
- OpenStreetMap is the default provider.\n
- Alternative providers (Google Maps, Mapbox) are allowed ONLY if explicitly requested by the user.\n

text.description:

raw_tools.name: hosting_clearWebsiteCacheV1

updated and needs to be visible immediately, or after making major changes.

Also purges the Hostinger CDN cache when CDN is enabled on the website. For a WordPress
installation living in a subdirectory, pass the directory query parameter to clear its cache.

testing changes, debugging issues, or when real-time updates must be visible. Disable it after
finishing development work to restore the performance benefits of caching.

raw_tools.name: hosting_toggleWebsiteCacheV1
raw_tools.description:
Turns server-side caching for the website on or off, based on the enabled flag. Enable it for
faster page loads, reduced server load, and improved user experience; recommended for production
websites. Disabling may impact performance; to temporarily bypass caching while developing or
debugging, prefer toggling cacheless mode instead.

Does nothing if caching is already in the requested state.

Skip this verification when using Hostinger's free subdomains (*.hostingersite.com).

raw_tools.name: hosting_listNodeJSBuildsV1
raw_tools.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of Node.js build processes for a specific website.

Each build represents a single run of the Node.js build pipeline. Use the `states`
query parameter to filter results by build state (pending, running, completed, failed).
Use the `uuid` from a build to poll its output via the `Get Node.js Build Logs` endpoint.

states.description: Build states to filter by

raw_tools.name: hosting_createNodeJSBuildFromArchiveV1
raw_tools.description:
Upload a project archive, auto-detect build settings, and immediately start a Node.js build.

This is the recommended single-step approach for deploying a Node.js application.
The archive is uploaded to the website's file storage, build settings are auto-detected
from the package.json inside the archive, and the build process starts automatically.
Optional override fields take precedence over auto-detected values.
Maximum archive size is 50MB.

Before archiving, exclude `node_modules/` and any build output directories
(e.g. `dist/`, `.next/`, `build/`) — they are not needed because the build
process runs the install step automatically, and including them unnecessarily
increases the archive size. This also helps keep the archive well under the 50MB limit.

Example (zip):
```
zip -r archive.zip . --exclude "node_modules/*" --exclude "dist/*"
```

The returned build `uuid` can be used to poll progress and retrieve logs via
the `Get Node.js Build Logs` endpoint.

node_version.description: Node.js version override (auto-detected from package.json if omitted)

root_directory.description: Application root directory override (where package.json is located) relative to public_html

output_directory.description: Build output directory override relative to the root directory

raw_tools.name: hosting_getNodeJSBuildLogsV1
raw_tools.description:
Retrieve logs from a specific Node.js build process.

To stream live output while a build is running, poll this endpoint repeatedly
while the build state is `running`, passing the previously returned `lines` count
as `from_line` to fetch only new output since the last call.
Log content may contain ANSI escape sequences (color codes).

from_line.description: Line from which to start retrieving logs

raw_tools.name: hosting_restartNode_jsApplicationV1
raw_tools.description:
Restarts the Node.js server process for the website. Does not rebuild or redeploy the
application. Use it to apply environment or configuration changes, or to recover a hung
application.

Only applicable to server-side applications (Express, Next.js, NestJS, etc.). Static
front-end apps (React, Vue, Vite) have no persistent server process, so restarting them
has no effect. Returns success even when the website has no server process to restart.

raw_tools.name: hosting_createWebsiteV1
raw_tools.description:
Create a new website for the authenticated client.

Provide the domain name and associated order ID to create a new website.
The datacenter_code parameter is required when creating the first website
on a new hosting plan - this will set up and configure new hosting account
in the selected datacenter.

Subsequent websites will be hosted on the same datacenter automatically.

Website creation takes up to a few minutes to complete. Check the
websites list endpoint to see when your new website becomes available.

domain.description: Domain name for the website. Cannot start with "www."

datacenter_code.description: Datacenter code. This parameter is required when creating the first website on a new hosting plan.

raw_tools.name: hosting_deleteWebsiteV1
raw_tools.description:
Permanently deletes a website and all of its data. This action is destructive
and cannot be undone. Always ask the user for explicit confirmation before
calling this endpoint.

All website files, databases and related configuration will be removed.
The hosting plan itself is kept, so a new website can be created on it afterwards.

The confirm field must be boolean true, otherwise the request is rejected.

Supported websites: main and addon domain websites on web hosting plans, and
Website Builder websites. Parked domains and subdomains cannot be deleted with
this endpoint. The domain must be the exact website domain, not a preview
domain or an alias.

Returns 404 when the domain does not exist or does not belong to the
authenticated client.

Website removal is processed asynchronously and can take a few minutes to
complete. The response returns before the removal finishes.

raw_tools.name: agencyHosting_deployNodeStaticWebsite
raw_tools.description: Deploy a node-static Agency Plan (h5g) website from an archive file. WARNING: this overwrites the website's existing contents and cannot be undone — always confirm with the user before proceeding. Use this for Agency Plan websites of type node-static (a Node.js-built static site that requires a build step or a plain simple static site). The tool resolves the website from its domain, uploads the archive to the website's file browser over TUS, and triggers the build-assets process which builds the site and deploys the result to public_html. This operation is synchronous: the build and deployment complete before the tool returns, so the website is live as soon as the tool finishes successfully — there is no separate asynchronous build to wait for or poll. For plain PHP applications that should be extracted as-is, use agencyHosting_deployPhpApplication instead. The website UID is automatically resolved from the domain.

The tool resolves the website from its domain, uploads the archive to the website's file browser over TUS, and triggers the import-archive process which overwrites the website contents with the archive contents. This operation is synchronous: the archive is extracted and deployed before the tool returns, so the website is live as soon as the tool finishes successfully — there is no separate asynchronous build to wait for or poll. For node-static websites that require a build step, use agencyHosting_deployNodeStaticWebsite instead. The website UID is automatically resolved from the domain.

raw_tools.name: horizons_createWebsiteV1
raw_tools.description:
Create new Hostinger Horizons website from the given message.\n
Use this tool when user asks you to create a website, landing page, blog
or any other type of application.\n
This tool initiates the website creation process and returns a website URL and ID.
The generation happens asynchronously.\n
After invoking this tool, your chat reply must be EXACTLY 1 sentence summarizing
that Hostinger Horizons is now creating their website and it will be ready in a few minutes
and you should provide the website URL to the user immediately
Do not write code.\n\nTo edit afterwards, users must go to Hostinger Horizons interface
in the provided website URL.
If the tool call fails with an error, you should provide a clear explanation of the error
and do not generate code yourself in the chat.
\n
TECHNOLOGY STACK CONSTRAINTS (STRICTLY ENFORCED):\n
The environment is limited to the following technologies.
You MUST NOT use, suggest, or implement any technology outside this list:\n
\n
- Language: JavaScript ONLY.
- Languages like TypeScript, Rust, Python, Java, PHP, etc., are STRICTLY PROHIBITED.\n
- Framework: React.\n
- Navigation: React Router.\n
- Styling: TailwindCSS.\n
- Components: shadcn/ui (built with @radix-ui primitives).\n
- Icons: Lucide React.\n
- Animations: Framer Motion.\n
\n
BACKEND & DATA STORAGE:\n
- Horizons integrated backend is the EXCLUSIVE solution for persistent data storage,
authentication, and database needs.\n
- Local databases (SQLite, MySQL, etc.) are STRICTLY PROHIBITED.\n
- Third-party services (Firebase, AWS Amplify) are allowed ONLY if explicitly requested by the user.\n
\n
MAPS:\n
- OpenStreetMap is the default provider.\n
- Alternative providers (Google Maps, Mapbox) are allowed ONLY if explicitly requested by the user.\n

text.description:

raw_tools.name: hosting_createNodeJSBuildFromArchiveV1
raw_tools.description:
Upload a project archive, auto-detect build settings, and immediately start a Node.js build.

This is the recommended single-step approach for deploying a Node.js application.
The archive is uploaded to the website's file storage, build settings are auto-detected
from the package.json inside the archive, and the build process starts automatically.
Optional override fields take precedence over auto-detected values.
Maximum archive size is 50MB.

Before archiving, exclude `node_modules/` and any build output directories
(e.g. `dist/`, `.next/`, `build/`) — they are not needed because the build
process runs the install step automatically, and including them unnecessarily
increases the archive size. This also helps keep the archive well under the 50MB limit.

Example (zip):
```
zip -r archive.zip . --exclude "node_modules/*" --exclude "dist/*"
```

The returned build `uuid` can be used to poll progress and retrieve logs via
the `Get Node.js Build Logs` endpoint.

node_version.description: Node.js version override (auto-detected from package.json if omitted)

root_directory.description: Application root directory override (where package.json is located) relative to public_html

output_directory.description: Build output directory override relative to the root directory

raw_tools.name: hosting_getNodeJSBuildLogsV1
raw_tools.description:

raw_tools.description:

raw_tools.name: hosting_deleteWebsiteV1
raw_tools.description:
Permanently deletes a website and all of its data. This action is destructive

Website Builder websites. Parked domains and subdomains cannot be deleted with
this endpoint. The domain must be the exact website domain, not a preview
domain or an alias.

authenticated client.

Website removal is processed asynchronously and can take a few minutes to
complete. The response returns before the removal finishes.

raw_tools.description:
Create new Hostinger Horizons website from the given message.\n
Use this tool when user asks you to create a website, landing page, blog
or any other type of application.\n
This tool initiates the website creation process and returns a website URL and ID.
The generation happens asynchronously.\n
After invoking this tool, your chat reply must be EXACTLY 1 sentence summarizing
that Hostinger Horizons is now creating their website and it will be ready in a few minutes
and you should provide the website URL to the user immediately
Do not write code.\n\nTo edit afterwards, users must go to Hostinger Horizons interface
in the provided website URL.
If the tool call fails with an error, you should provide a clear explanation of the error
and do not generate code yourself in the chat.
\n
TECHNOLOGY STACK CONSTRAINTS (STRICTLY ENFORCED):\n
The environment is limited to the following technologies.
You MUST NOT use, suggest, or implement any technology outside this list:\n
\n
- Language: JavaScript ONLY.
- Languages like TypeScript, Rust, Python, Java, PHP, etc., are STRICTLY PROHIBITED.\n
- Framework: React.\n
- Navigation: React Router.\n
- Styling: TailwindCSS.\n
- Components: shadcn/ui (built with @radix-ui primitives).\n
- Icons: Lucide React.\n
- Animations: Framer Motion.\n
\n
BACKEND & DATA STORAGE:\n
- Horizons integrated backend is the EXCLUSIVE solution for persistent data storage,
authentication, and database needs.\n
- Local databases (SQLite, MySQL, etc.) are STRICTLY PROHIBITED.\n
- Third-party services (Firebase, AWS Amplify) are allowed ONLY if explicitly requested by the user.\n
\n
MAPS:\n
- OpenStreetMap is the default provider.\n
- Alternative providers (Google Maps, Mapbox) are allowed ONLY if explicitly requested by the user.\n

type.description: type parameter

text.description:
Detailed project specification.
Include purpose, key features, user flows, data models, and design preferences.
The specification should be detailed and comprehensive, covering all aspects of the project.

raw_tools.name: hosting_listNodeJSBuildsV1
raw_tools.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of Node.js build processes for a specific website.

Each build represents a single run of the Node.js build pipeline. Use the `states`
query parameter to filter results by build state (pending, running, completed, failed).
Use the `uuid` from a build to poll its output via the `Get Node.js Build Logs` endpoint.

states.description: Build states to filter by

raw_tools.name: hosting_createNodeJSBuildFromArchiveV1
raw_tools.description:
Upload a project archive, auto-detect build settings, and immediately start a Node.js build.

This is the recommended single-step approach for deploying a Node.js application.
The archive is uploaded to the website's file storage, build settings are auto-detected
from the package.json inside the archive, and the build process starts automatically.
Optional override fields take precedence over auto-detected values.
Maximum archive size is 50MB.

Before archiving, exclude `node_modules/` and any build output directories
(e.g. `dist/`, `.next/`, `build/`) — they are not needed because the build
process runs the install step automatically, and including them unnecessarily
increases the archive size. This also helps keep the archive well under the 50MB limit.

Example (zip):
```
zip -r archive.zip . --exclude "node_modules/*" --exclude "dist/*"
```

The returned build `uuid` can be used to poll progress and retrieve logs via
the `Get Node.js Build Logs` endpoint.

node_version.description: Node.js version override (auto-detected from package.json if omitted)

root_directory.description: Application root directory override (where package.json is located) relative to public_html

output_directory.description: Build output directory override relative to the root directory

raw_tools.name: hosting_getNodeJSBuildLogsV1
raw_tools.description:
Retrieve logs from a specific Node.js build process.

To stream live output while a build is running, poll this endpoint repeatedly
while the build state is `running`, passing the previously returned `lines` count
as `from_line` to fetch only new output since the last call.
Log content may contain ANSI escape sequences (color codes).

from_line.description: Line from which to start retrieving logs

raw_tools.name: hosting_restartNode_jsApplicationV1
raw_tools.description:
Restarts the Node.js server process for the website. Does not rebuild or redeploy the
application. Use it to apply environment or configuration changes, or to recover a hung
application.

Only applicable to server-side applications (Express, Next.js, NestJS, etc.). Static
front-end apps (React, Vue, Vite) have no persistent server process, so restarting them
has no effect. Returns success even when the website has no server process to restart.

raw_tools.name: hosting_listNode_jsVulnerabilitiesV1
raw_tools.description:
Lists known npm package vulnerabilities detected on a Node.js website, enriched with
advisory metadata (severity, CVSS score, CVE, advisory URL). Results are sorted from
the most severe to the least severe, then by publish date (newest first). Use the
`severities` query parameter to filter.

Vulnerabilities with `is_patchable` set to `true` can be auto-fixed via the
`Patch Node.js Vulnerabilities` endpoint, which opens a GitHub pull request with
updated package versions. Auto-fix is only available for websites deployed from a
connected GitHub repository. Vulnerabilities with `is_patching_in_progress` set to
`true` are already included in an open patch pull request; while any patch pull
request is open, new patch requests for this website are rejected until it is merged
or closed.

Data comes from periodic dependency scans, so it may lag behind the latest deployment.
An empty list means the most recent scan found no vulnerabilities; it does not
guarantee the current deployment is vulnerability-free. Available on Business and
Cloud Hosting plans.

raw_tools.name: hosting_patchNode_jsVulnerabilitiesV1
raw_tools.description:
Patches the selected Node.js vulnerabilities by updating the affected package versions
in `package.json` and opening a GitHub pull request in the connected repository. The
customer reviews and merges the pull request; merging triggers the automatic deployment.

Auto-fix is only available for websites deployed from a connected GitHub repository.
Websites deployed from an archive have no auto-fix path and return a 404. The Hostinger
GitHub App needs write access to the repository; without it the request fails with a
403 explaining the missing permission.

Only vulnerabilities with `is_patchable` set to `true` can be patched. Non-patchable
IDs in the selection are skipped; the pull request covers the patchable subset, listed
in `patched_vulnerability_ids`. Selections without any patchable vulnerability are
rejected with a 422. Only one patch pull request can be open at a time per website;
close or merge it before patching again. Available on Business and Cloud Hosting plans.

vulnerability_ids.description: List of vulnerability IDs to patch, as returned by the list vulnerabilities endpoint.

raw_tools.name: hosting_createWebsiteV1
raw_tools.description:
Create a new website for the authenticated client.

Provide the domain name and associated order ID to create a new website.
The datacenter_code parameter is required when creating the first website
on a new hosting plan - this will set up and configure new hosting account
in the selected datacenter.

Subsequent websites will be hosted on the same datacenter automatically.

Website creation takes up to a few minutes to complete. Check the
websites list endpoint to see when your new website becomes available.

raw_tools.name: hosting_deleteWebsiteV1
raw_tools.description:
Permanently deletes a website and all of its data. This action is destructive
and cannot be undone. Always ask the user for explicit confirmation before
calling this endpoint.

All website files, databases and related configuration will be removed.
The hosting plan itself is kept, so a new website can be created on it afterwards.

The confirm field must be boolean true, otherwise the request is rejected.

Supported websites: main and addon domain websites on web hosting plans, and
Website Builder websites. Parked domains and subdomains cannot be deleted with
this endpoint. The domain must be the exact website domain, not a preview
domain or an alias.

Returns 404 when the domain does not exist or does not belong to the
authenticated client.

Website removal is processed asynchronously and can take a few minutes to
complete. The response returns before the removal finishes.
